text: After this the Lord chose seventy-two more followers and sent them ahead of him in pairs, to every town and place he himself planned to visit.
He told them: the harvest is huge but the workers are few, so ask the Lord of the harvest to send out more workers.
Go, he said — I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
Carry no purse, no bag, no sandals, and don't stop to greet people along the road.
Whatever house you enter, first say, 'Peace to this house.'
If a peaceable person lives there, your peace will rest on them; if not, it will return to you.
Stay in that same house, eating and drinking whatever they give you, since a worker deserves wages — don't move from house to house.
When you enter a town and they welcome you, eat what's set before you.
Heal the sick there and tell them, 'The kingdom of God has come near to you.'
But if a town does not welcome you, go into its streets and say,
'We wipe off even the dust of your town that clings to our feet as a warning against you — yet know this: the kingdom of God has come near.'
I tell you, Sodom will fare better on judgment day than that town.
Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! If the miracles done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
Tyre and Sidon will fare better at the judgment than you will.
And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No — you will be brought down to the depths.
Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me — and rejects the one who sent me.
The seventy-two came back overjoyed, saying, 'Lord, even the demons obey us in your name!'
He replied, 'I watched Satan fall like lightning from heaven.'
'I have given you authority to walk over snakes and scorpions and over all the enemy's power; nothing will hurt you.'
'But don't celebrate that the spirits obey you — celebrate that your names are written in heaven.'

At that moment, full of joy in the Holy Spirit, Jesus said: I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, for hiding these things from the wise and learned and revealing them to little children — yes, Father, this was your good pleasure.
Everything has been entrusted to me by my Father. No one truly knows the Son except the Father, and no one truly knows the Father except the Son and those the Son chooses to show him to.
Then, turning to his disciples privately, he said, 'Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.'
'Many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see and never saw it, and to hear what you hear and never heard it.'
Just then an expert in the law stood up to test Jesus: 'Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?'
Jesus answered, 'What is written in the Law? How do you read it?'
The man replied: 'Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, strength, and mind — and love your neighbor as yourself.'
'You've answered correctly,' Jesus said. 'Do this and you will live.'
But wanting to justify himself, the man asked, 'And who is my neighbor?'
Jesus replied: A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when robbers attacked him, stripped him, beat him, and left him half dead.
A priest happened to be going down the same road; when he saw the man, he crossed to the other side and passed by.
A Levite did the same — came to the spot, saw him, and passed by on the other side.
But a Samaritan, traveling that way, came upon the man, and when he saw him he was moved with compassion.
He went to him, bandaged his wounds, pouring oil and wine on them, then put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
The next day he handed the innkeeper two silver coins and said, 'Look after him, and I'll repay you for any extra expense when I come back.'
'Which of these three,' Jesus asked, 'do you think acted as a neighbor to the man who fell among robbers?'
The expert said, 'The one who showed him mercy.' Jesus told him, 'Go and do the same.'
As they continued on, Jesus entered a village where a woman named Martha welcomed him into her home.
She had a sister named Mary, who sat at the Lord's feet listening to what he was saying.
But Martha was pulled in every direction by the serving; she came to Jesus and said, 'Lord, don't you care that my sister has left me to do all the work myself? Tell her to help me.'
'Martha, Martha,' the Lord answered, 'you are worried and upset about so many things.'
'But only one thing is truly needed. Mary has chosen the better part, and it will not be taken from her.'
